name: Hotel d'Inghilterra
positioning: A 16th-century Roman residence turned hotel, in the heart of Rome's fashion district between Via Condotti and Via Frattina
best_for: Travelers who want a historic base within walking distance of the Spanish Steps and the Trevi Fountain
Couples looking for suites with a balcony or private terrace over Rome's rooftops

facts.text: The hotel is in the heart of Rome's fashion district, between Via Condotti and Via Frattina.
The Trevi Fountain and the Spanish Steps are each about a five-minute walk away.
The hotel is a 16th-century Roman residence turned into a hotel.
The hotel's history is tied to the noble Torlonia family.
Rooms and suites feature refined fabrics, original furnishings and works of art.
The Balcony Suites have a balcony overlooking Rome's rooftops.
The Spa Suite offers massages inspired by traditional Eastern treatments.
Guests can learn about the art of Roman micromosaic at the Le Sibille workshop, one of the hotel's Craft Experiences.
Café Romano Lounge Bar is one of Rome's oldest hotel bars.
Café Romano has a terrace on Via Borgognona.
The hotel has a library with a checkerboard desk and burnt-orange sofas.

highlights.text: Terrazza Romana is a sixth-floor rooftop cocktail bar with views over the rooftops of Rome.
Many rooms and suites have views of Villa Medici, the Vittoriano and the church of San Carlo.
Past guests have included Mark Twain, Henry James, Elizabeth Taylor and Gregory Peck.
Second-floor rooms and suites feature vintage William Morris wallpapers the design team found in the basement.
The Penthouse Suite has a private terrace with a view of the city.

considerations.text: This is a city-centre hotel in Rome's busy fashion district, not a resort.
Two street-level entrances have wheelchair ramps, and lifts reach all floors.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing reflecting the luxury positioning.
